title: Python SDK: human-friendly streaming API + event-dispatch primitives for chat completions
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Deliver a small, ergonomic Python surface around chat completion streaming that: exposes an idiomatic async iterator for tokens/segments, provides a first-class event-dispatch primitive for non-token events (tool calls, metadata, errors), documents a clear backpressure contract for consumers, and includes examples and tests showing retry behavior on transient network frames. The goal is to reduce user-side boilerplate and make common patterns (partial render, incremental evaluation, deterministic restore after retry) straightforward.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Initial ticket created after design sync with DX and API teams. Key constraints: must be backwards-compatible with existing sync/simple streaming call patterns, and the core HTTP/WS transport should remain unchanged (we wrap it with ergonomics only).

2026-03-04 - Priya Reddy: Spike complete. Implemented a PoC generator-based async iterator that yields TokenEvent and NonTokenEvent objects. Found that interleaving tool-call events during token emission was the trickiest UX; proposed a single Event base with a 'kind' discriminator and convenience helpers (is_token(), as_text()).

2026-03-06 - Jordan Kim (review): Architectural feedback - prefer small immutable event dataclasses and a thin EventDispatcher that maps user handlers to event kinds. Raised concern about garbage creation under high-throughput; suggested pooling / reusing lightweight Token segments or exposing raw bytes option for extreme perf paths.

2026-03-08 - Priya Reddy: Implemented backpressure example where consumer can call 'await iterator.pause()' and 'iterator.resume()' — this is an advanced API behind a flag (experimental=True) to avoid surprising users. Basic use remains simple: 'async for ev in client.stream_chat(...): if ev.is_text(): print(ev.text)'.

2026-03-10 - Design feedback (Asha Patel): UX sign-off on event naming and examples. Requested an example showing a GUI incremental renderer + cancel/rollback semantics when a retry happens mid-stream. Added follow-up to add a small reference app under examples/streaming_chat_ux.py.

2026-03-11 - Priya Reddy: Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/612. PR includes: Event dataclasses, AsyncStreamIterator wrapper, EventDispatcher helper, README examples, unit and integration tests emulating transient 5xx frames with retry middleware.

2026-03-12 - Security review (Nina Cho): No PII flows introduced; recommended adding a note about how partial transcript caching should be controlled for regulated customers. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Santos: Performance microbenchmark: generator wrapper adds ~2-3% overhead for typical 8k-token sessions; acceptable for ergonomic wins. Noted that high-QPS customers should use the raw streaming interface (documented in README) or enable pooled token buffers.

2026-03-14 - Priya Reddy: Addressed review comments on PR, added example for deterministic retry where consumer replays last stable checkpoint on transient error. Ready for final review and merge gating once QA verifies flaky network test matrix.
